findings.title: `float: right` on .small-action button no longer works now that .small-action is a flex container
findings.body: `.small-action` was turned into a flex container (`@include flexbox()` at line 264), which makes `float` a no-op on all of its direct children. The `button { ... float: right; }` rule at line 306-310 (used for the small-action action buttons, e.g. undo/delete) will therefore no longer be pushed to the right edge; it will sit immediately after `.small-action-desc` in normal flex order. The same applies to `.topic-avatar { float: left; }` (line 270), which is now dead code. To keep the button right-aligned, use `margin-left: auto` on the button (or `flex: 1` on `.small-action-desc`) instead of a float.

findings.title: order() mixin maps modern `order` values directly onto 1-based legacy ordinal-group properties
findings.body: `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group` (old 2009 flexbox spec) are 1-based and default to 1, while the modern `order` property is 0-based and defaults to 0. Emitting the same raw `$val` for both means legacy WebKit/Gecko engines see an ordering that is shifted by one relative to modern engines, and `@include order(0)` would emit the invalid `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: 0`. If the legacy prefixes are intended to work, the mixin should emit `$val + 1` for the ordinal-group properties.

findings.title: align-items() mixin is inconsistent with flexbox() and will emit invalid legacy values for flex-start/flex-end/stretch
findings.body: `flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box` for legacy Gecko, but `align-items()` has no `-moz-box-align`, so legacy Gecko gets the old box display with no alignment. Additionally, `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` only accept the old keywords (`start`, `end`, `center`, `baseline`, `stretch`); calling `@include align-items(flex-start)` or `align-items(flex-end)` — the normal modern values — would produce invalid legacy declarations that are silently dropped, making the prefixed fallbacks useless for those values. Either translate the values inside the mixin or drop the legacy prefixes.

findings.title: Header .panel right-alignment relies on `margin-left: auto`, unsupported by the legacy box fallbacks added in the same PR
findings.body: `.panel` lost `float: right` and now relies on `margin-left: auto` plus `order: 3` to be pushed to the right of `.contents`. Auto margins for free-space distribution are a modern flexbox feature; in the legacy `-webkit-box` / `-moz-box` modes that `flexbox()` deliberately emits as fallbacks, `margin-left: auto` does not consume free space, so in those engines the header panel (user/notifications/search icons) will no longer be right-aligned — it will sit directly after the title. If those fallbacks are meant to be functional, use `-webkit-box-flex`/spacer handling or drop the legacy display values.

findings.title: Percentage padding on .small-action-desc makes text indentation viewport-dependent
findings.body: `.small-action-desc` changed from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `padding: 0 1.5%`. Percentage padding resolves against the containing block's width, so the horizontal inset now varies with the topic/viewport width instead of being a fixed, font-relative amount; combined with the fact that `.small-action-desc` is a flex item with no `flex` value (so it only takes its content width), the text position and wrapping of small-action messages will be inconsistent across widths. A fixed em/px padding plus `flex: 1` would be more predictable.
